bites.title: Paint and polish
bites.body: A material decides how a surface handles light: its color, whether it's metal, how rough or glossy it is.

bites.title: Look properly
bites.body: Z, then Material Preview, so you can actually see materials.

bites.title: A new material
bites.body: In Properties, click the red checkered ball tab (Material), then click New.
bites.hint: The material tab is near the bottom of the Properties tab column.

bites.title: Name it
bites.body: Double-click the material's name at the top of the tab and call it Clay. Materials get reused, so names matter.

bites.title: Pick a color
bites.body: Click the Base Color swatch and pick anything bold.
bites.hint: The Base Color bar is near the top of the Surface panel. Click it for the color wheel.

bites.title: Make it metal
bites.body: Drag Metallic all the way to 1.

bites.title: Polish it
bites.body: Set Roughness down to 0.1. Rough is matte, smooth is a mirror.

bites.title: Two materials, one object
bites.body: Tab into Edit Mode, press 3, click one face. In the Material tab press the + beside the slot list, click New, then click Assign.
bites.hint: Three steps: + adds a slot, New fills it, Assign paints the selected faces with it.

bites.title: Lesson 08: cleared
bites.body:
New materials, base color, metal, roughness, and multiple materials on one mesh.

Reward: the Shader Editor just slid in at the bottom. It's the same material, drawn as a node graph. Scroll on for Lesson 09.
